plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets and parks turn lavender-purple as this tree's trumpet-shaped flowers open in huge clusters over feathery, fern-like leaves. When the blooms fall, they carpet the pavement in violet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly October to December
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and Sydney and Brisbane, Australia
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America. Its seeds are held in flat, round pods that rattle in the wind, and the tree now lines city streets on several continents.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: Chrysanthemums fill autumn gardens with dense, layered pompoms and spidery blooms. They are at their best when other flowers are fading, and cool nights bring out rich colour.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn, typically September to November in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across Japan, China, Europe and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Japan holds chrysanthemum festivals every autumn, and the flower is a symbol of the Imperial family. Each bloom is really a cluster of many tiny flowers called florets.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: Delicate, open-faced blossoms with golden stamens appear on glossy evergreen shrubs as the weather cools. Their light fragrance and cheerful colour brighten gardens when many plants are going dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, about October to December
plants.location: Southeastern United States, such as Georgia and the Carolinas, and southern Japan
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Its seeds are pressed to make camellia oil, which is used in cooking and cosmetics in Asia.
